rhymes.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star

lines.meaning_en: A little star shines brightly.

lines.text: How I wonder what you are!
lines.speech: How I wonder what you are!
lines.meaning_en: I think about what the star really is.

lines.text: Up above the world so high,
lines.speech: Up above the world so high,
lines.meaning_en: It is very high above the world.

lines.text: Like a diamond in the sky.
lines.speech: Like a diamond in the sky.
lines.meaning_en: It sparkles like a diamond in the sky.

rhymes.source: Traditional nursery rhyme, first verse only. The words come from the poem 'The Star' by Jane Taylor, published 1806 (author known, long out of copyright, public domain). The tune is a traditional French melody and is NOT provided in the app.
rhymes.picture_concept: A big friendly yellow star with a smiling glow in a dark blue night sky, small stars around, a tiny village or hill below.

items_to_review: copyright status confidence: high, not legally verified

rhymes.title: Baa, Baa, Black Sheep

lines.meaning_en: Someone speaks to a black sheep.
Do you have any wool?
The sheep answers politely: yes.
It has enough wool to fill three bags.

rhymes.source: Traditional English nursery rhyme, first four lines of the first verse (earliest printed version 1744, authorship unknown, public domain). Melody not provided.
rhymes.picture_concept: A fluffy black sheep standing in a green field, smiling, with three bags of wool beside it.

items_to_review: parents may prefer a different colour word; wording kept traditional

rhymes.title: Humpty Dumpty

lines.text: Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall,
lines.speech: Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall,
lines.meaning_en: Humpty Dumpty, an egg-shaped character, sat on a wall.

lines.text: Humpty Dumpty had a great fall.
lines.speech: Humpty Dumpty had a great fall.
lines.meaning_en: He fell down badly.

lines.text: All the king's horses and all the king's men
lines.speech: All the king's horses, and all the king's men,
lines.meaning_en: All of the king's horses and soldiers
could not fix him and put him back together.

rhymes.source: Traditional English nursery rhyme, first printed 1797, authorship unknown, public domain. Melody not provided.
rhymes.picture_concept: A smiling egg character with little arms and legs sitting on a brick wall, a horse and a soldier looking on kindly (gentle, no distress).

items_to_review: picture must keep the fall gentle for young children

rhymes.title: Jack and Jill

lines.text: Jack and Jill went up the hill
lines.speech: Jack and Jill went up the hill
lines.meaning_en: Two children walked up a hill.

lines.text: To fetch a pail of water.
lines.speech: To fetch a pail of water.
lines.meaning_en: They went to get a bucket of water.

lines.text: Jack fell down and broke his crown,
lines.speech: Jack fell down and broke his crown,
lines.meaning_en: Jack fell and hurt his head ('crown' means the top of the head).
Jill fell down after him.

rhymes.source: Traditional English nursery rhyme, first verse only (known from the 1760s, authorship unknown, public domain). Melody not provided.
rhymes.picture_concept: A boy and a girl climbing a green hill carrying a wooden pail, a well at the top, cheerful mood.

items_to_review: 'crown' and 'pail' are old words; parent may need to explain

rhymes.title: Row, Row, Row Your Boat

lines.meaning_en: Push your boat along with oars.
Go softly down the river.
Happily, happily, happily, happily,
Life is like a happy dream.

rhymes.source: Traditional children's song; words first published 1881 (credited to Eliphalet Oram Lyte in that publication; long out of copyright, public domain). Melody not provided.
rhymes.picture_concept: A small boat on a calm river with two oars, a child rowing, soft morning light.

items_to_review: existing boat.png fitness to be confirmed by a person looking at it

rhymes.title: Itsy Bitsy Spider

lines.text: The itsy bitsy spider climbed up the waterspout.
lines.speech: The itsy bitsy spider climbed up the waterspout.
lines.meaning_en: A tiny spider climbed up a water pipe.

lines.text: Down came the rain and washed the spider out.
lines.speech: Down came the rain, and washed the spider out.
lines.meaning_en: Rain fell and washed the spider down.

lines.text: Out came the sun and dried up all the rain,
lines.speech: Out came the sun, and dried up all the rain,
lines.meaning_en: The sun came out and dried the rain.

lines.text: And the itsy bitsy spider climbed up the spout again.
lines.speech: And the itsy bitsy spider climbed up the spout again.
lines.meaning_en: The spider climbed up the pipe once more.

rhymes.source: Traditional children's song (American wording, 'itsy bitsy'; British 'incy wincy'), first verse only, in circulation since the early 1900s, authorship unknown, public domain. Wording has regional variants; this is the common US form. Melody not provided.
rhymes.picture_concept: A tiny smiling spider climbing a red water pipe; rain on the left half of the picture, a bright sun on the right half.

items_to_review: copyright status confidence: high, not legally verified

rhymes.title: చిట్టి చిలకమ్మ

lines.meaning_en: Little parrot, did Mother hit you?
Did you go to the garden and bring a fruit?
Did you put it in the nest, or gulp it down?

rhymes.source: Traditional Telugu folk children's rhyme, as commonly sung; no single author known to me. Exact wording has variants. Confidence that it is folk/public domain: medium-high (a film song with a similar opening may exist; not checked). Melody not provided.
rhymes.picture_concept: A small green parrot with a red beak holding a fruit near a nest in a garden tree; a mother bird nearby.

items_to_review: exact traditional wording and spelling of all 3 lines
whether 'Mother hit you' tone suits young children

rhymes.title: చందమామ రావే

lines.meaning_en: Moon, please come.
Little moon, please come.
Climb the hill and come.
Bring gogu (roselle) flowers.

rhymes.source: Traditional Telugu lullaby, authorship unknown, folk / public domain (widely known; many longer versions exist, only the opening four short lines used). Confidence in wording: medium-high. Melody not provided.
rhymes.picture_concept: A big smiling full moon rising behind a hill, a mother and baby looking up, small flowers in the foreground.

items_to_review: exact traditional wording of the 4 lines
new blank చందమామ and distractors కుర్చీ / చెప్పు (revised after verifier REVISE)
word 'గోగుపూలు' in the last line may still be unfamiliar; native educator to confirm

rhymes.title: పిల్లి కుక్క

lines.meaning_en: Cat, cat, meow meow,
drank milk and went to sleep.
Dog, dog, bow-wow,
is guarding the house.

rhymes.source: original, written for Aksharamala (not a traditional rhyme). Written by the content-creator agent; has had no human or native review.
rhymes.picture_concept: A cat curled up asleep next to a bowl of milk, and a dog sitting at a house door on guard. (Existing cat.png covers only the cat; a dog should be added.)

items_to_review: grammar and natural flow of all 4 lines (original text)

rhymes.title: चंदा मामा दूर के

lines.meaning_en: Uncle Moon, who lives far away,
cooked sweet puas made with sugar,
you eat from a plate,
and give the baby his share in a small cup.
The cup broke,
and the baby sulked.

rhymes.source: Traditional Hindi folk lullaby, authorship unknown, public domain as far as I know. Wording has variants ('बूर' is powdered sugar; some versions say 'भूर' or differ in later lines). Melody not provided.
rhymes.picture_concept: A smiling moon uncle in the night sky holding a plate of puas, a baby below looking up with a small cup.

items_to_review: exact wording and spelling (बूर / भूर, मुन्ने / मुन्ना)

rhymes.title: आलू कचालू

lines.text: आलू कचालू बेटा कहाँ गए थे
lines.speech: आलू कचालू, बेटा कहाँ गए थे?
lines.meaning_en: Potato-boy, my child, where did you go?

lines.text: बैंगन की टोकरी में सो रहे थे
lines.speech: बैंगन की टोकरी में सो रहे थे।
lines.meaning_en: I was sleeping in the brinjal basket.

lines.text: बैंगन ने लात मारी रो रहे थे
lines.speech: बैंगन ने लात मारी, रो रहे थे।
lines.meaning_en: The brinjal kicked me, so I was crying.

lines.text: मम्मी ने प्यार किया हँस रहे थे
lines.speech: मम्मी ने प्यार किया, हँस रहे थे।
lines.meaning_en: Mummy gave me a hug and I was laughing.

rhymes.source: Traditional Hindi children's rhyme, authorship unknown, folk / public domain as far as I know. Wording has regional variants. Confidence in exact wording: medium. Melody not provided.
rhymes.picture_concept: A cheerful little potato character leaving a basket of brinjals, a mother hugging a laughing child.

items_to_review: exact wording / which version is standard

rhymes.title: चिड़िया रानी

lines.meaning_en: Queen bird, chirp chirp chirp,
eats grain,
drinks water,
and flies away with a whoosh.

rhymes.source: original, written for Aksharamala (not a traditional rhyme). Written by the content-creator agent; has had no human or native review.
rhymes.picture_concept: A small colourful bird eating grains, then drinking from a clay bowl, then flying up; three small panels.

rhymes.title: நிலா நிலா ஓடி வா

lines.meaning_en: Moon, moon, come running,
come running without stopping,
climb up the hill and come,
bring jasmine flowers.

rhymes.source: Traditional Tamil children's rhyme as commonly taught. I believe it is folk, but I am NOT certain no named author is credited in some collections; wording has variants (e.g. 'மலை மேலே' / 'மலை மேல'). Confidence in copyright-free status: medium. Melody not provided.
rhymes.picture_concept: A smiling round moon rolling down a hill toward a child holding a string of jasmine flowers.

rhymes.title: கை வீசம்மா கை வீசு

lines.meaning_en: Swing your arms, swing your arms,
we can go to the shop, swing your arms,
we can buy sweets, swing your arms,
we can eat them slowly, swing your arms.

rhymes.source: Traditional Tamil children's action rhyme, authorship unknown to me, folk / public domain as far as I know. Wording has variants. Confidence in wording: medium-high. Melody not provided.
rhymes.picture_concept: A child walking happily with arms swinging toward a small village shop with jars of sweets.

rhymes.title: பூனைக்குட்டி நாய்க்குட்டி

lines.meaning_en: Kitten, meow meow,
drinks the milk, meow meow.
Puppy, bow-wow,
guards the house, bow-wow.

rhymes.source: original, written for Aksharamala (not a traditional rhyme). Written by the content-creator agent; has had no human or native review.
rhymes.picture_concept: A kitten drinking milk from a bowl and a puppy sitting by a house door. (Existing cat.png covers only the cat; a puppy should be added.)
